title: Effective discrete-modulated continuous variable QKD under general attacks
authors: Mariana Navarro, Antonio Acín, Carlos Pascual-García
abstract: Continuous variable quantum key distribution via discrete modulations ensures information-theoretic security using standard telecom technologies, providing affordable and scalable quantum communications with simplified classical postprocessing. However, existing security proofs against general attacks often rely on restrictive assumptions, such as a bounded dimension for coherent states, or require impractically large block sizes. In this work, we develop a finite-size security analysis that removes these limitations while incorporating realistic experimental features. Our approach combines the dimension reduction technique, a security proof based on the marginal-constrained entropy accumulation, and a trusted detector model accounting for the receiver imperfections. We report positive key rates in the finite-size regime for relevant block sizes of the order of $10^8$. These results contribute to narrowing the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical implementations of discrete-modulated continuous variable quantum key distribution protocols.
summary: The paper presents a robust finite-size security analysis for discrete-modulated CVQKD protocols. It overcomes limitations of previous proofs by integrating dimension reduction and using the MEAT framework. The results confirm positive key rates for realistic block sizes, advancing the field toward practical quantum communication.
main_problem: The work develops a finite-size security analysis for discrete-modulated continuous variable Quantum Key Distribution (CVQKD) protocols under general attacks.
main_result: Positive key rates are reported in the finite-size regime for relevant block sizes on the order of $10^8$, successfully bridging the gap between theoretical proofs and practical implementations.
method: The security analysis combines dimension reduction, a proof based on the Marginal-Constrained Entropy Accumulation Theorem (MEAT), and modeling receiver imperfections using a trusted detector model.
model_or_system: The system is CVQKD utilizing discrete modulations of coherent states, modeled by discretizing phase space measurements into finite registers ($Z_j$). The analysis framework extends established quantum information security metrics ($\epsilon$-security).
key_observables: Secret key rate (bits/pulse), dimension reduction penalty ($\zeta_\alpha$), and the final achievable key length $\ell$.
important_parameters: Block sizes ($n \sim 10^8$ to $10^{10}$), modulation parameters ($\Delta, \Delta_s$), detection efficiency ($\eta_d$), and reconciliation efficiency ($ eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on continuity bounds to justify dimension reduction from infinite-dimensional states to finite subspaces, and uses the MEAT framework.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase space representation of modulations (Figure 1) and show the dependence of the dimension reduction penalty ($\zeta_\alpha$) and the final finite-size secret key rates on channel transmittance ($\chi$) for various block sizes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the discrete protocol, formalizing security using $\epsilon$-security metrics, developing mathematical tools like concentration inequalities, and finally applying MEAT combined with dimension reduction to derive a rigorous lower bound on the secret key rate.
why_interesting: This work provides advanced theoretical tools for quantifying security in practical quantum communication systems, which is crucial for realizing scalable quantum networks.
